Deriving the Chain Rule  When we have a function that is a composition of two or more functions, we could use all of the techniques we have  already learned to differentiate it. However, using all of those techniques to break down a function into simpler parts that  we are able to differentiate can get cumbersome. Instead, we use the chain rule, which states that the derivative of a  composite function is the derivative of the outer function evaluated at the inner function times the derivative of the  inner function.
